min_stable_gain.conditions: p1 'Decompensated, gain >= 7 V/V (stable)'; p18 phase margin at noise gain 7 V/V (16.9 dB) close to 55 deg across temperature (SIM, Figs 8-5/8-6); PM < 0 deg at gain 1 (p18)
min_stable_gain.below_min_gain_guidance: Gains below 7 give more peaking and possible instability (p23). Noise-gain shaping (9.2.1, p22-24): the example is G = -2 V/V with RG = 226 ohm, a 62 ohm termination and RF = 453 ohm, giving an LF noise gain of 2.79 V/V (Eq 1). Adding 2.7 pF from the inverting node to ground and 0.5 pF across RF cuts the peaking from about 13 dB (Fig 9-6) to less than 1.5 dB (Fig 9-7, measured and simulated). Design rules: the zero is at 1/(2 pi (RF||RG) CIN) (Eq 2) and the pole at 1/(2 pi RF CF) (Eq 3). The pole must fall before |AOL| = |1/beta|, with about 20 dB/decade rate of closure. Reference: AN-1604. For a TIA, the HF noise gain is set by input capacitance / feedback capacitance, so the amplifier need not be unity-gain stable (p18).

current_noise.hf_behavior: rising about +20 dB/decade (proportional to f) from about 1 MHz to 100 MHz (53 fA -> 0.52 pA -> 4.65 pA per rtHz); slope eases to about +15 dB/decade between 200 and 960 MHz. Below 100 kHz the slope is about +6 to +13 dB/decade.
current_noise.how_measured_or_defined: p19 8.3.5: CMOS/JFET input impedance exceeds several GOhm at low frequency, which eliminates bias current and its shot noise. At higher frequencies the transistor's parasitic capacitance to drain, source and substrate lowers the impedance, and the input current noise increases 'as a result of capacitive coupling between the CMOS gate oxide and the underlying transistor channel ... a natural artifact of the construction of the transistor and is unavoidable'. One curve is given for both inputs (I_BN and I_BI). The datasheet does not say whether it is measured or simulated.

tia_content.notes: Place an isolation resistor R_ISO of 10-20 ohm close to IN- to damp the trace-inductance resonance; close the R_F/C_F/R_ISO loop at the APD pins (p27, Figs 9-10/9-11). Trace inductance isolates the APD capacitance from the noise gain (Eq 4, NG = 1 + Z_F/Z_IN).

application_guidance: Single 3.3-5.25 V or split supplies; inputs and outputs are not rail-to-rail (p25). Cut the power and ground planes under the signal I/O pins. Bypass with 100 pF-0.1 uF C0G/NPO within 0.25 in, plus 2.2-6.8 uF bulk. Use low-reactance SMT resistors placed close to the pins, with the feedback and series output resistors near the output. Connect PD to VS+ to enable. The NC pin isolates FB from IN-. Connect the thermal pad to the negative supply pin (p26 Fig 9-9). PD thresholds are referenced to VS-: on 3.3 V/GND, disable < 0.65 V and enable > 1.8 V; on +/-2.5 V, -1.85 V and -0.7 V (p20). In power-down the output is high impedance, and an input difference above a diode drop opens a low-impedance path from IN+ to the output (p20-21).
abs_max_and_input_protection: VS total 5.5 V; inputs (VS-)-0.5 to (VS+)+0.5 V; differential input 1 V; output (VS-)-0.5 to (VS+)+0.5 V; continuous input current +/-10 mA; continuous output current +/-100 mA; TJ 150 C; storage -65 to 150 C. ESD HBM 1000 V, CDM 1500 V (p5). ESD diodes on all pins to both supplies; two anti-parallel diodes between the inputs clamp over-range or fault inputs (p17, Fig 8-3).
other_notes: Contradiction: Fig 6-10 (p9) open-loop magnitude is about 4 dB above Fig 8-5/8-6 (p18) and above the table GBWP. By the datasheet's own method (f at 60 dB x 1000), Fig 6-10 gives 8.8 GHz and Fig 8-5 gives 5.7 GHz; the table gives 5.5 GHz. Fig 8-5/8-6 are described as simulations; Fig 6-10's origin is not stated. The p18 phase margin of 55 deg at noise gain 7 matches Fig 8-5, not Fig 6-10, whose phase reads about 72 deg at the 16.9 dB crossover.
Fig 9-3 legend reads 'C_F = 1 pF / 2 pF' but the text and the data (which coincide with Fig 9-2 at C_PD = 1 and 2 pF) indicate C_PD.
HD2/HD3 table entries are printed as positive dBc numbers. The table HD2 at 10 MHz (-88 dBc, 5 V single supply) is about 11 dB worse than the Fig 6-13 curve (-99.5 dBc, +/-2.5 V).
The table 0.1 dB flatness of 130 MHz is lower than the Fig 6-7 curve, which stays within +0.1 dB to about 197 MHz.
The p1 headline bias current of 10 pA does not match the table (0.4 pA typ, 5 pA max).
The Fig 8-7 (Z_OL) and Fig 8-8 (current noise) curves are identical in the OPA858 and OPA859 datasheets.
Turn-on 13 ns, turn-off 120 ns (p7). PD pin bias current 70 uA typ (p7).
